messages:
alex: Heads-up — the new sample-app we shipped for edge runtimes is failing in Cloudflare workers: `TypeError: require is not defined` when importing the SDK.
ellie: Oh no. Which build did the sample use? The CJS bundle by accident?
rahul: I noticed this too when testing the worker sample locally. package.json was pointing at `main` -> dist/index.cjs.js but the worker runtime expects ESM imports.
morgan: This smells like our dual-pkg publish defaults. We currently publish both CJS and ESM but the conditional exports don't include the edge-specific path so bundlers/edge see the CJS entry.
alex: Here's the minimal repro package.json snippet we used in the sample app (from the published tarball):
```json
{
  "name": "redwood-sample-edge",
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.esm.js",
  "exports": {
    "./package.json": "./package.json",
    "import": "./dist/index.esm.js",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js"
  },
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts"
}
```
ellie: That `exports` shape is OK, but Cloudflare/deno resolvers sometimes ignore `import`/`require` conditionals and pick `main` or `module` heuristics. Also some bundlers still resolve `main` first.
rahul: There's another issue: our published tarball is missing the ESM .map files and the `package.json` in the tarball has `main` top-level which many packagers treat as the authoritative entry.
morgan: Proposal: make the edge-friendly behavior explicit — add an `exports` condition like `{ "edge": "./dist/edge.mjs", "import": "./dist/index.esm.js", "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js" }` and publish an `edge.mjs` that uses only fetch-compatible APIs.
nina: That works but also needs typings coverage. TS consumers in ESM land expect `types` to point at an ESM-friendly declaration. Right now our `dist/index.d.ts` references Node builtins (fs/stream) via conditional types which breaks in Deno.
alex: Related pain: auth/retry behavior differs between Node and edge bundles. Node SDK uses node-fetch + native TLS + our auth cache, edge bundle uses `fetch` and a lightweight retry wrapper — subtle differences in backoff and credential refresh flow caused a 401 in a sample during a retry race.
ellie: We should document the parity matrix for runtime differences (Node vs Edge vs Deno). Also add a smoke test in the sample-app CI that runs the worker on `miniflare` or `deno test` so we catch these early.
rahul: Agreed. Actionable items: 1) Add `exports.edge` entry and publish edge.mjs; 2) Ensure `types` are portable (avoid Node-only refs or provide a separate `types-edge.d.ts`); 3) Add CI smoke for Cloudflare/Miniflare + Deno.
morgan: I'll draft a tiny PR for package.json change and add an extra artifact `dist/edge.mjs`. Can we also gate an npm alias so the sample-app installs `@redwood/sdk-edge` until we validate?
alex: That would be safest for onboarding. New users hitting the sample should get a working import out of the box.
dev-bot: deploy-notify: created branch `devex/edge-sample-fix` and assigned to morgan.
nina: One more DX nit — our Quickstart code snippets in docs mix `import Redwood from 'redwood'` and `import { Redwood } from 'redwood'`. On edge builds default exports may be tree-shaken differently. We should standardize examples to named imports to avoid ambiguity.
ellie: +1 standardize and add a short paragraph on "Which build to use" for customers: node — use `@redwood/sdk`; edge/deno — use `@redwood/sdk-edge` (temporary) or `import` with `exports.edge` present.
rahul: I'll add the smoke tests and a matrix job in GH actions. If we add edge-specific package, we should also ensure our `release` script populates the right files.
morgan: Starting work now, will ping when PR is up for review. If anyone wants to help with the Deno typings audit please DM.
alex: Thanks — this should reduce onboarding friction for the sample apps and clear up a bunch of support tickets. :thumbsup:
